name: generated-ui
cost: Free and bundled with Qwen Code. You bring your own model provider and API key
works_with: Qwen Code, in Web Shell or the Desktop app
short: Shows an interactive calculator, simulator or comparison right in the chat, for jobs like splitting a bill or comparing plans.
what: When you want to change numbers and see what happens, the agent builds a small interactive card in the conversation instead of writing an HTML file. It passes HTML, CSS and JavaScript to a `generated_ui_show` tool. The script runs in an isolated QuickJS worker with no network, files or browser access. Each card carries a written summary of the result and its assumptions, so the answer still reads without the interface.
who: Qwen Code users working in Web Shell or the Desktop app. It isn't offered in the terminal UI, headless `qwen -p` runs, editor clients or chat channels, so skip it if that's where you work.
needs: Qwen Code, viewed in Web Shell or the Desktop app
Node.js 22 or newer if you install with npm
A model provider and API key, set up with `/auth`

steps.title: Install Qwen Code
steps.text: Linux and macOS. Restart your terminal afterwards.

steps.title: Set up a model
steps.text: Run it in your project, then run `/auth` to choose your provider and API key.

steps.title: Open a client that shows cards
steps.text: Generated UI is bundled and on by default where cards can render: Web Shell (`qwen serve --open`, experimental) or the Desktop app.

steps.title: Ask for something to adjust
steps.text: Ask for a calculator, simulator or comparison where you want to try different numbers.

try.label: From the README
try.where: Qwen Code Web Shell or Desktop
try.text: Ask it to help split a bill, or to compare two plans with weights you can drag.

watch: The Linux and macOS install pipes a script from the internet straight into your shell. Read the script first, or use npm or Homebrew.
Cards can't fetch data, open files or act for you. Errors that only appear after you change inputs aren't caught before display.
To turn it off, set `experimental.generatedUi` to `false` and restart the CLI or daemon session.
